newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Ethiopian troops said to seize Somali Islamic base.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian troops said to seize Somali Islamic base.

text.p: Ethiopian troops backed by tanks captured an Islamic stronghold deep inside Somalia on Thursday, a fundamentalist group said in the capital.
An aid worker in neighbouring Kenya said the offensive against the town of Luq began on Wednesday night.
A spokesman for al-Ittihad al-Islam (Islamic Unity) in Mogadishu reported the fall of Luq, the group's main centre about 100 km (60 miles) from the Ethiopian border.
Ethiopia sent troops into the same area twice last year, calling al-Ittihad a "multinational terrorist group", but had never previously taken Luq.
In Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital, a foreign ministry official declined to comment. Ethiopia has in the past refused to discuss similar operations until they are over.

Al-Ittihad's spokesman, Ahmed Bile Hassan, told Reuters the group's militiamen were resisting the Ethiopian offensive. But he said they had retreated from Luq and that Bulo Hawo, near the three-sided border Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya, had also been captured.
"There is a strong suspicion of Ethiopian military involvement," aid worker Katie Downie of the African Medical and Research Foundation (AMREF) told Reuters in Nairobi.
Downie said AMREF headquarters had no radio contact with its health project office in Luq on Thursday. She said reports from the area indicated Luq had been captured.
Aid sources believed the Ethiopian offensive was probably done in tandem with Omar Haji's Somali National Front (SNF), a group opposed to al-Ittihad.
"Since August last year, the SNF has built up its army quite substantially," one aid source said.
Until Wednesday night Ethiopian forces had remained stationary about 20 km (12 miles) inside Somalia since their last incursion last December.
Unconfirmed reports from the border area reaching Mogadishu said Ethiopian troops were backed by up to 25 tanks and armoured vehicles.
